testName: Class B Knowledge Test #1 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: An empty truck:

options.text: Stops in a shorter distance than a full truck.
Stops in a longer distance than a full truck.
Stops in the same distance as a full truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stops in a longer distance than a full truck.
questions.explanation: Empty trucks need a longer stopping distance than full trucks because they have less weight for traction.

questions.question: When checking power steering fluid during a vehicle inspection, which is NOT required?

options.text: Show where the power steering fluid dipstick is located.
Check that there is enough power steering fluid.
Ensure the power steering fluid level is above the full mark.
Ensure the power steering level is above the refill mark.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ensure the power steering fluid level is above the full mark.
questions.explanation: During the vehicle inspection test, you must show where the dipstick is and confirm there is enough fluid. The level must be above the refill mark, not the full mark.

questions.question: How should you hold the steering wheel?

options.text: With one hand, keeping the other hand free.
With one hand at a time, switching hands.
At the base of the wheel.

questions.explanation: Always hold the steering wheel firmly with both hands on opposite sides of the wheel.

questions.question: When leaving your vehicle, you should:
questions.explanation: Always apply the parking brake when you leave your vehicle.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT part of an air brake system?
questions.explanation: An air brake system includes an air compressor, gauges, storage tanks, drains, a safety valve, a brake pedal, foundation brakes, warning devices, and spring brakes. An air filter is not part of the air brake system.

questions.question: How much water is needed on a road for hydroplaning to happen?
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning occurs when tires lose grip on the road and slide on a layer of water. Only a small amount of water is needed for this to happen.

questions.question: If hydraulic brakes fail, you can slow down by:

options.text: Letting the truck run out of gas.

questions.explanation: If your hydraulic brakes fail, shift into a lower gear to help slow your vehicle.

questions.question: Before driving downhill, you should:

options.text: Take your vehicle out of gear.

questions.explanation: Always shift into a lower gear before going downhill to avoid overusing your brakes.

questions.question: Once stopped during the stop/start maneuver, you should:

options.text: Keep the vehicle in first gear.

questions.explanation: When you park during the stop/start maneuver, apply the parking brake. Shift into neutral or park. You must park parallel to the curb and not block any driveways or intersections.

questions.question: When entering a foggy area, you should:

options.text: Stop on the side of the roadway.

questions.explanation: Slow down before entering a foggy area. Use low beam headlights, do not pass other vehicles, and do not stop on the side of the road. If possible, avoid driving in fog.

questions.question: When a trailer starts to turn while backing, you should follow it by:

options.text: Doing nothing. The vehicle will follow naturally.
Turning the steering wheel in the opposite direction.
Turning the steering wheel farther in the same direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turning the steering wheel in the opposite direction.
questions.explanation: When backing with a trailer, turn the steering wheel the opposite way from where you want the trailer to go. Once the trailer starts turning, turn the steering wheel the other way to follow it.

questions.question: Without engine oil, what happens?

options.text: A vehicle will use less fuel.
An engine can be destroyed quickly.
An Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) will not work properly.

questions.correctAnswerText: An engine can be destroyed quickly.
questions.explanation: Engine oil is critical for engine protection. Without it, an engine can be destroyed very quickly.

questions.question: Why is backing with a trailer dangerous?

options.text: It is hard to see behind the vehicle.
Most trucks cannot move in reverse.
Cargo may fall out of the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is hard to see behind the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Backing a truck is always dangerous because the driver cannot see everything behind them. You should avoid backing whenever possible.

questions.question: During the driving test, when asked to change lanes, what should you do?

options.text: Do not worry about other drivers.
Use your turn signal and change lanes when it is safe.
Change lanes as quickly as possible, even if it means cutting off another driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your turn signal and change lanes when it is safe.
questions.explanation: When changing lanes during the driving test, check your mirrors, use your turn signal, and change lanes smoothly when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: Loading cargo with a high center of gravity:

options.text: Makes the vehicle more likely to roll over.
Makes items more likely to fall down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Makes the vehicle more likely to roll over.
questions.explanation: Cargo with a high center of gravity increases the risk of a rollover. Always load cargo so the weight is balanced and low.

questions.question: Most heavy trucks with manual transmissions need ____ to change gears.
questions.explanation: Most heavy trucks with manual transmissions require double clutching to shift gears. This takes practice to do well.

questions.question: Before you go downhill, you should:

options.text: Take your vehicle out of gear.
Use only your brakes to slow down.

questions.explanation: On a steep hill, use the engine's braking power to control your speed. Shift down before going downhill. If you rely only on brakes, they can overheat and stop working.

questions.question: Air pressure in a single air system should build from 50 to 90 psi within:
questions.explanation: In a single air system, air pressure should build from about 50 to 90 psi in three minutes.

questions.question: You must use at least ____ to secure cargo on a flatbed trailer.
questions.explanation: Use at least one tie-down for every 10 feet of cargo. All cargo, no matter how small, must have at least two tie-downs.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT a distracted person that drivers should worry about?

options.text: A driver talking to a passenger
A child on the side of the road
A construction worker on the side of the road
A person sitting on a bench waiting for a bus

questions.correctAnswerText: A person sitting on a bench waiting for a bus
questions.explanation: Be careful around people not paying attention to the road. Watch for road workers, drivers talking to passengers, and children near the road.

questions.question: A 10-foot load must be secured with at least ____ tie-downs.
questions.explanation: On flatbed trailers, cargo must be tied down. Use at least one tie-down for every 10 feet of cargo. Always use at least two tie-downs, no matter the cargo size.

questions.question: Poor weight balance:

options.text: Makes a vehicle harder to handle.
Makes a vehicle easier to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Makes a vehicle harder to handle.
questions.explanation: Unbalanced weight makes a vehicle unsafe and difficult to control.

questions.question: Don't stare at one mirror too long because:

options.text: Looking at mirrors can make you drowsy.
You may drive far without looking at the road.
The mirror may not show the road accurately.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may drive far without looking at the road.
questions.explanation: Check mirrors often but quickly. Staring at one mirror too long means you are not watching the road ahead.

questions.question: Using a hand-held cell phone while driving is:

options.text: Allowed if the weather is clear.

questions.explanation: Using a hand-held cell phone while driving is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: During a vehicle inspection, you must identify all of the following, except:
questions.explanation: Check the power steering belt, water pump belt, alternator belt, and air compressor belt for cracks or frays. If any are not belt-driven, tell the examiner and verify they work properly and are not damaged.

questions.question: Steering wheel play should be no more than:
questions.explanation: A steering wheel should have no more than 10 degrees of play, which is about two inches of movement on a 20-inch wheel. Too much play makes steering difficult.

questions.question: To use stab braking, you should:

options.text: Push the brakes fully until the wheels lock, release until wheels roll, then repeat.
Push the brakes halfway while keeping the wheels rolling.
Push the brakes fully until the wheels lock and the vehicle stops.
Use the emergency brake until the vehicle slows.

questions.correctAnswerText: Push the brakes fully until the wheels lock, release until wheels roll, then repeat.
questions.explanation: Stab braking means pushing the brakes all the way until they lock. Then release them until the wheels roll again. Repeat this pattern.

questions.question: Dry bulk tanks require special care because:

options.text: They have low centers of gravity.
They have high centers of gravity.

questions.correctAnswerText: They have high centers of gravity.
questions.explanation: Dry bulk tanks have high centers of gravity and their loads often shift during travel. Be extra careful when turning and taking curves.

questions.question: During a trip, gauges are:

options.text: The only way to know about vehicle problems.
One way to know about vehicle problems.

questions.correctAnswerText: One way to know about vehicle problems.
questions.explanation: Check gauges, mirrors, tires, cargo, and lights during your trip to spot any problems early.

questions.question: Rims with welding repairs:

options.text: Are safe to use on the rear of the vehicle.
Are safe to use with a light load.

questions.explanation: Wheels or rims with welding repairs are never safe and should not be used.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a sign of tire failure?
questions.explanation: When a tire fails, you may hear a loud bang or feel heavy thumping and vibration in your vehicle. If steering feels heavy or the rear of your vehicle fishtails, stop to check your tires.

questions.question: When doing pre-trip inspections:

options.text: Do the same checks in the same order every time.
It is okay to check items in a different order each time.
You do not need to check every item each time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do the same checks in the same order every time.
questions.explanation: Always do pre-trip inspections the same way each time. This helps you remember to check all important items.

questions.question: Vehicles with Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS) have ____ warning lights that show when the ABS is not working.
questions.explanation: Vehicles with ABS have yellow warning lights to alert you when the braking system is not working. Know where this light is on your vehicle before you start driving.

questions.question: For an offset back/right parking maneuver, you should:

options.text: Drive straight forward, then back up to the right.
Drive straight forward, then back up to the left.
Drive forward to the right, then back up straight.
Drive forward to the left, then back up straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive straight forward, then back up to the right.
questions.explanation: For an offset back/right maneuver, drive straight forward first, then back up to the right. Your vehicle must be fully within the parking space boundaries.

questions.question: When should you slow down for a curve?
questions.explanation: Slow to a safe speed before you enter a curve. Slowing down while in the curve can cause a skid.

questions.question: What can happen if the exhaust system does not work properly?

options.text: Poisonous fumes may enter the cab.
Fumes may come out the back of the muffler.

questions.correctAnswerText: Poisonous fumes may enter the cab.
questions.explanation: Exhaust system leaks are very dangerous. They can allow toxic fumes into the cab or sleeper area, which can harm the driver and passengers.

questions.question: ____ is a thin, clear layer of ice that forms on road surfaces.
questions.explanation: Black ice is a thin, clear layer of ice. You can see the road through it, which makes it look like the road is just wet.

questions.question: The most important reason to inspect your vehicle before a trip is:
questions.explanation: The most important reason to inspect your vehicle is to keep yourself and others safe on the road. State and federal laws require vehicle inspections before every trip.

questions.question: After changing a tire, the driver should stop a short distance later to:

options.text: Check that the lug nuts are tight.
Make sure the tire tread is good.
Confirm the correct tire was changed.
Check if rocks are in the tread.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check that the lug nuts are tight.
questions.explanation: Stop a short time after changing a tire to re-check that all lug nuts are tight.

questions.question: A vehicle inspection is required:
questions.explanation: State and federal laws require drivers to inspect their vehicles before every trip.

questions.question: A driver with an open window in cold weather may be:
questions.explanation: Watch other drivers for signs of impairment. Drivers who are drunk, tired, on drugs, or sick can be dangerous. An open window in cold weather is one sign a driver may be impaired.

questions.question: On the driving test, you will be graded on lane usage. Which is an example of poor lane usage?

options.text: Not driving over curbs or sidewalks
Using the leftmost lane when more lanes are available
Ending a right turn in the rightmost lane

questions.correctAnswerText: Using the leftmost lane when more lanes are available
questions.explanation: On the driving test, do not cross curbs, sidewalks, or lane markings. Stop behind stop lines, crosswalks, or stop signs. On multi-lane roads, turn in the correct lane. Always use or stay in the rightmost lane unless blocked.

questions.question: Good drivers look ____ seconds ahead of their vehicles.
questions.explanation: Good drivers look 12 to 15 seconds ahead. This gives you time to react to hazards before you reach them.

questions.question: Most heavy vehicles require ____ to change gears.
questions.explanation: Most heavy vehicles with manual transmissions use double clutching. Release the accelerator, push in the clutch, and shift to neutral at the same time. Release the clutch and let the vehicle reach the right speed. Then push in the clutch, shift gears, and release the clutch while accelerating.

questions.question: Bracing is used to:

options.text: Make items stand taller in a trailer.
Keep items from moving in a trailer.
Make it easier to unload items from a trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep items from moving in a trailer.
questions.explanation: Blocking and bracing stop cargo from shifting during transport. Blocking is placed in front, back, and sides. Bracing goes from the top of cargo to the trailer floor and walls.

questions.question: When making tight turns, a driver should:

options.text: Open their door for a better view.

questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often while driving. Pay special attention to your mirrors when changing lanes, turning, merging, or making tight turns.

questions.question: Stopping distance can be affected by:
questions.explanation: Stopping distance depends on your vehicle's speed, weight, and road traction.

questions.question: If you hear or feel something unusual while driving, you should:

options.text: Hope the vehicle lasts until someone else drives it.
Stop and check it out to find a solution.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and check it out to find a solution.
questions.explanation: Use your senses while driving to spot mechanical problems. If you see, hear, smell, or feel anything wrong, stop and check it.

questions.question: A driver can have:

options.text: Two licenses—one for cars and one for trucks.
One license for each state where they plan to drive.
A car license from one state and a CDL from another.

questions.explanation: You cannot have more than one license. States share driver information through a computer system to prevent duplicate licenses.

questions.question: How often should you drain air tanks with manual drains?
questions.explanation: Drain air tanks with manual drains at the end of each day. This prevents oil and water from building up in the tanks.
